title: New model intake: lightweight checklist, smoke-tests, and risk ledger
body:
Purpose:
A compact, operational intake checklist and smoke-test plan for new model candidates (open and checkpointed) to be used by model owners and Applied ML reviewers. The goal is to get a high-confidence go/no-go for serving experiments within 5 working days for low-risk models and 10 working days for higher-risk candidates. This is intentionally lightweight — favors fast feedback and a clear owner for each step.

Quick summary of workflow (1-line):
1) Owner flags model -> 2) Run automated harness + smoke set -> 3) Human spot-checks -> 4) Risk ledger triage -> 5) Canary/metric gate or reject.

Minimum deliverables from model owner (required to start intake):
- model artifact location (s3/GCS): path and sha256
- model card draft: architecture, training data summary, license, quantization plan
- intended use cases and latency/throughput targets (p50/p95 target on Redwood infra)
- primary point-of-contact and backup (name + slack + email)

Lightweight intake checklist (tick boxes for reviewer)
- [ ] Repo + artifact verified (owner provided checksum and manifest)
- [ ] Model loads in eval-harness container (no OOM) using conftest v2
- [ ] Baseline smoke prompts run (see "smoke prompt set")
- [ ] Critical safety probes executed (toxicity, PII leakage quick checks)
- [ ] Cost/latency estimate captured (in tokens/sec and $/1M tokens)
- [ ] Owner assigned rollout plan: canary route and fallback model variant
- [ ] Risk ledger entry created and triaged

Smoke prompt set (for initial human + automated checks)
- intent classification samples (10): short queries across intents for calibration
- instruction-following probes (15): varying length and multimodal hints (if applicable)
- safety probes (12): adversarial prompts, data exfil attempts (PII pattern checks)
- regression sentinel prompts (10): owner-provided prompts that exercise business logic
- evaluation harness config: length cap = 256, sampling = greedy and top-p=0.95 (for stochastic models run 3 seeds)

Automated harness commands (example)
- docker run --rm -v $PWD:/work eval-harness:latest python run_eval.py --model-uri s3://models/new-candidate --prompts smoke_prompts.json --out results/smoke.json
- python scripts/quick_metrics.py results/smoke.json --metrics latency,throughput,token-usage,bleu,rouge

Pass/fail success criteria (fast gate; owner must provide fixes if failed)
- Functional: model must complete generation for 100% of smoke prompts within memory budget (no OOM)
- Latency: p50 < owner-target * 1.2 and p95 < owner-target * 1.5 (unless owner requests relaxed latency for very high-quality model)
- Quality (heuristic): automated quality heuristics must not be worse than baseline model on regression sentinels (baseline defined in intake ticket). If automated heuristics flag regressions, manual review required.
- Safety: no prompt in safety probe set should return explicit PII (SSN/email of private individuals) and toxicity heuristic score must be <= threshold (configurable per team).

Risk ledger (create an entry per candidate) - quick template to copy into the shared Risk doc:
- Candidate: <model-name>@<sha>
- Owner: <name>
- Risk level: low | medium | high (initial estimate)
- Known gaps: data provenance, rare-token hallucination, unsupported tokensets
- Mitigation plan: canary, rate-limiting, latency-based fallback, human-in-loop for certain routes
- Decision: allow-canary | require-fallback | block

Manual spot-check guidance (2 reviewers recommended):
- Each reviewer does a 20-minute pass: cover conversational threads, instruction tasks, and safety probes.
- Log interesting failures to the ticket with example input/output and tags (safety, factuality, formatting, hallucination).

Owners & RACI (short):
- Model owner (responsible): builds artifact, supplies model card, fixes regressions (example: Priya Shah)
- Applied ML reviewer (accountable): runs harness, signs off on smoke tests (example: Diego Alvarez)
- SRE/Infra (consulted): capacity/latency estimate and infra deployment constraints (example: Owen Hart)
- Product/PM (informed): business impact and rollout gating (example: Maya Li)

Escalation paths and timelines:
- If safety probe fails -> immediate hold, escalate to security/compliance and product within 24h.
- If automated regressions detected -> owner has 48h to respond with mitigation or new artifact, otherwise intake is paused.
- If latency or infra constraints exceed estimates -> infra consult within 72h, possible deferral to Dedicated pool.

Canary plan (recommended template):
- Start with 1% of traffic for 24-48h with detailed tracing tags (owner route + model variant).
- Monitor: token-level cost, latency p50/p95, user-visible error rate, eval-sentinel pass-rate.
- Roll forward to 10% then 50% with 24h stability gates. Automatic rollback on metric regression > X% (configurable per route).

Notes & open questions (for triage):
- Do we require a standardized model-card schema for all private intake? (proposal: yes, v0 minimal fields enforced.)
- Should we centralize safety probe library per vertical? (benefit: consistent coverage; cost: maintenance)
- How to handle chained models (retrieval + reranker + generator) in a single intake ticket? (proposal: allow composite intake with clear owner for each stage)

Next steps checklist for owner once initial smoke passes:
- add sentinel set to continuous regression tests (git PR to eval-harness)
- draft rollout route config for Redwood Console (canary route name, fallback model id)
- schedule a 30-min post-canary review with product and infra

Appendix: example short judgement template (copy into ticket)
- Verdict: Accept-for-canary / Needs-work / Reject
- Rationale: 2–3 bullets summarizing primary reasons (latency, regression, safety)
- Action items: list of owner actions and due dates

This doc is intentionally terse — aim is to be a low-friction gate that captures the right signals and assigns clear owners. Keep feedback in the intake ticket and update the risk ledger entry as mitigations are implemented.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12 initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-20 added risk ledger template and escalation windows (Diego)
